newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm, except for gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm, except for gasoline.

text.p: Med oil products were firm, bar gasoline. Gasoline may find some support, but futures prices erased early gains and one trader saw two Italian combined cargoes being bought by a trader who was expected to be moving the product towards northwest Europe.
A turkish tender for up to two low octane cargoes for early to Mid September delivery is expected to close on Monday.
Naphtha markets appear to be improving liquidity with Egyptian product seen available, and more Skikda barrels seen emerging at the end of the month.
A trader bought a Skikda cargo from another trader on Thursday at a $3.75 a tonne over CIF high Med quotes.
Gas oil was firm. Attention focused on low sulphur material with Mediterranean refiners awaiting the introduction of low sulphur quotes on Monday.
Many traders said they expected low sulphur to trade at a premium of $12 to $13 over 0.2 percent for the rest of the year. Traders said a French refiner had been buying heavily in the Med.
Russia was steady with cargoes being offered at quotes cif high +$2.50, basis Genoa. Demand from Turkey and Greece was seen supporting prices.
High sulphur cracked fuel remained firm with prices holding around the mid $90s fob. Dealers said getting hold of good quality material, especially bunker spec was difficult.

The Portuguese buy tender for six cargoes went to one trader at around mean fob NWE, mean fob Med +10.60. There were no details of the optional two cargoes in October. Dealers felt most of the product would have to come from NWE rather than the thin Med. The low sulphur cracked market was firm and although no interest was seen from the main Med buyer, traders speculated as to whether spot deals at been done discreetly. A trader was looking for 50,000 tonnes at $105.50 fob NWE.
